clue.text: Figure refuse should fetch money

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a figure
ash is the refuse left after burning

explanation.surface: A bin collection that somehow brings in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is ready money in notes and coins.

clue.text: The beauty appears to accept wrinkles

indicators.note: to accept means the appearing word takes the wrinkles inside it

parts.note: comes means appears, arrives
lines are wrinkles on the face

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman seems to come to terms with her wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: Comeliness is attractiveness, good looks.

clue.text: Returning seamen receiving little money for fish

indicators.note: receiving means the turned word takes the coin inside it
returning means the sailors word is written back to front

parts.note: tars are sailors
P is a penny, a small sum

explanation.surface: Sailors coming home get paid a pittance for their catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns TARS into SRAT, which takes P.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Fool superior politician into making an informed guess

parts.note: an ass is a fool
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, superior
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: making here means forming the letters of the word into into something new

explanation.surface: A snobbish MP is manipulated into guessing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' looks like a verb, but it is a noun here; 'superior' is the old U-and-non-U label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An assumption is a supposition reached from what one knows, an educated guess.

clue.text: Spot non-drinking egghead getting involved in dispute

indicators.note: getting involved in means these pieces go inside the dispute word

parts.note: to spar is to argue or dispute
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: A sober intellectual joins in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatter is to splash with spots or drops.

clue.text: Creating appalling din, true, but only at the experimental stage

indicators.note: appalling, dreadful, signals that din and true are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A terrible racket is made, but the idea is still being trialled.
explanation.definitionFit: Untried means not yet tested or proven.

clue.text: Increased turnover just the same

indicators.note: turnover just the same says the letters read identically when turned around

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Sales rose, yet takings stayed level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business talk, but it means reversing the whole answer, which is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised prices have been increased.

clue.text: Cover a single nurse can change

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, is a single

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the letters of nurse can into another order

explanation.surface: A lone nurse may provide cover by swapping shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance gives financial protection, called cover.

clue.text: Bearing with a pressman causing distress

parts.note: NE, north-east, is a compass bearing
ED, editor, is a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A reporter with a certain attitude causes upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Need can mean hardship or straits, as in those in need.

clue.text: The pains taken by a player

indicators.note: taken, as in taken apart, has the letters of the pains reworked

explanation.surface: An actor takes great trouble over the role.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, from Thespis of ancient Greek drama.

clue.text: Pole carrying bow quietly giving militaristic display

indicators.note: carrying means the pole word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a mast is a tall pole
an arch is a bow shape
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone holds a bow on a pole during a quiet military parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A march past is a parade of troops past a saluting dignitary.

clue.text: A quarter entering an art gallery will show a certain discrimination

indicators.note: entering means the quarter goes inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a well-known London art gallery
S, south, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A visitor arriving from one part of town at a gallery shows refined judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The TATE is London's national gallery of British and modern art.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is discernment in judging what is fine or fitting.

clue.text: A deal with the United States could be a bloomer

parts.note: a lot means a great deal
US is the usual abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A transatlantic trade deal might turn out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a flowering plant.

clue.text: Dancers unsure of their steps?

parts.note: dancers trip the light fantastic, and anyone unsure of footing may stumble

explanation.definitionFit: Trippers trip as they dance, and also trip up when they misstep.

clue.text: Showing spirit — game though dainty

parts.note: brandy is a distilled spirit
snap is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone shows spirit playing a game, though delicate.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAP is a children's card game; a brandy snap is a thin crisp rolled biscuit. 'dainty' is a noun here, a delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: This rolled ginger biscuit is a delicacy, a dainty treat.

clue.text: Breaking down in tears is not so good

indicators.note: breaking down means the letters of in tears are broken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Collapsing in tears is no improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning worse or less pleasant.

clue.text: Go round in pain, walking slowly

indicators.note: in means the turning word sits inside the pain word

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
to roll is to go round

explanation.surface: Someone hobbles around in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Strolling is walking at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: A fall in the German production of kitchen equipment

indicators.note: in means the fall word sits inside the German article

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: A downpour in Germany somehow yields a kitchen utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: A drainer is a rack or colander for letting washed things drip dry.

clue.text: The old-fashioned writer goes in for credits

indicators.note: goes in means the writer is placed within the two-letter word

parts.note: as can mean for, as in serving as
a scribe is a copyist of old

explanation.surface: A traditional author takes a bow when the credits roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe is to attribute, to credit something to someone.

clue.text: Shrub bearing white flowers used in pretty posy-ring arrangements

indicators.note: used in means the answer is found within the run of letters in posy-ring arrangements

explanation.surface: A flowering shrub suits pretty little floral rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangements' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters run straight across 'posy-ring a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the mock orange (also lilac), a shrub with fragrant pale blossom.

clue.text: More cross grain off with little hesitation

indicators.note: off, as in gone off, means the letters of grain are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: er is a brief hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Someone grows irritable when the corn goes bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Angrier is the comparative of angry, i.e. more annoyed.

clue.text: An upholder of the Christian word

definitions.text: An upholder of the Christian word

parts.words: An upholder of the Christian word
parts.note: reads like a defender of the faith, but means the stand that literally holds up the Bible in church

explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is the reading desk supporting the Bible in a church.

clue.text: A child gets absorbed in stories — and that's understatement

indicators.note: gets absorbed in means the child word goes inside the stories word

parts.note: stories can mean lies, fibs
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A youngster is engrossed in tales, which is putting it mildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech that affirms by denying the opposite, like not bad.

clue.text: Expressing approbation at finding everyone Conservative

parts.note: all means everyone
the right is the conservative side of politics

explanation.surface: Someone approves on discovering that everyone votes Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is acceptable or satisfactory signals approval.

clue.text: Once again put to sleep without point

indicators.note: without, in its old sense of outside, has the sleep word around the point

parts.note: rest means sleep
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: An animal is put down without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset is to set or place again.

clue.text: Mean in a devilish sort of way?

definitions.text: Mean in a devilish sort of way?

parts.words: Mean in a devilish sort of way?
parts.note: read as the manner of a small demon, an adverb formed from a little devil

explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to mean something without stating it, and an imp is a small devil.

clue.text: This factory might well go to pot!

definitions.text: This factory might well go to pot!

parts.words: This factory might well go to pot!
parts.note: go to pot means decay, but a garden specimen literally goes into a flowerpot; the word also means a factory

explanation.definitionFit: A plant is both an industrial works and a growing thing set in a pot.

clue.text: British holiday resort where there isn't a bar?

parts.note: O, nought, suggests nothing being there
a ban is a bar or prohibition

explanation.surface: A seaside town without a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: OBAN is a resort town on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a Scottish seaside town popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: The happy state of a man composing music

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ... was an English composer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means utter joy and is also the surname of the composer Arthur Bliss.

clue.text: At sea for the most part

definitions.meaning: out on the ocean, the main being the open sea

explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old word for the ocean, and the phrase also means mostly.

clue.text: The retiring fellow would never wear such a thing!

definitions.text: The retiring fellow would never wear such a thing!

parts.words: The retiring fellow would never wear such a thing!
parts.note: a shy man would shun frilly feminine wear, yet retiring also means going to bed, when a woman puts on her bedtime gown

explanation.definitionFit: This garment is a woman's gown worn for sleeping, so a man going to bed would not wear it.

clue.text: Staunch and high-minded individual given work

parts.note: ST, saint, is a person of lofty virtue
OP, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A loyal idealist is handed a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch a flow is to halt it.
